title: SLO-driven region affinity mesh with capacity guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: As Redwood’s hosted footprint grows, regional performance variability and intermittent capacity shortages are increasingly impacting customer SLOs. Current steering rules use a mix of static geo-preference and simple latency hedging but lack a single SLO-driven decision surface that balances latency targets, regional capacity headroom, and customer affinity.

Goal: Implement an SLO-driven region affinity mesh that: (1) routes requests primarily by SLO risk rather than raw latency; (2) respects soft geo-affinity (customer-configurable); (3) enforces capacity guardrails and circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent region overload; and (4) supports graceful load shedding strategies when total capacity is insufficient. The system must be observable, testable under chaos, and rolloutable via canary.

Scope: This ticket covers the design and MVP implementation of the routing decision engine and associated guardrails for the control plane and runtime hooks. It excludes autoscaler changes and dedicated capacity pricing adjustments, which are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane exposes a decision API that computes per-request routing weights using SLO risk, latency percentile deltas, and available capacity headroom
Runtime can accept weighted routing hints and fall back to safe-mode (nearest healthy region) when a region circuit breaker trips
Circuit breakers trip based on combined indicators: region CPU/GPU saturation, request queue growth, and sustained SLO breach probability
Load shedding supports two modes: deterministic token-based shedding (reserved tokens for P0 customers) and probabilistic shedding for best-effort traffic
End-to-end e2e tests demonstrate SLO preservation in a simulated 3-region outage with at least 90% of P95 latency SLOs met for premium customers
Dashboards and alerts for SLO risk, region headroom, circuit-breaker state, and shedding rates are published in Console and linked in the runbook
design_decisions: SLO signal: use running Bayesian estimate of SLO breach probability computed from p50/p95/p99 windows and recent error rates rather than a single latency threshold
Affinity: implement soft geo-affinity weights that apply a tunable penalty to non-preferred regions instead of hard pinning
Capacity headroom: compute effective headroom as a conservative percentile of recent available GPU slots + predicted short-term throughput from historical traffic patterns
Circuit breaker policy: two-tier breakers (fast path: per-host queue depth; slow path: region-level trending SLO risk), both must be green for routing into a region
Shedding strategy: preserve P0 customers with reserved token buckets; apply probabilistic shedding on lower tiers and degrade model size as last resort fallback
Fallback models: support automatic fallback to smaller/quantized model variants when region-level per-token latency is increasing to preserve throughput
implementation_plan: Week 0: Prototype decision function in runtime simulator (Python) using historical traces; produce initial SLO risk curves
Week 1: Implement control plane decision API and wire a beta flag to the router; build simple REST endpoint for weighted hints
Week 2: Add region-level circuit breaker integration and expose breaker state via control plane API
Week 3: Implement token bucket preservation for P0 and probabilistic shedding for other tiers in runtime request filter
Week 4: End-to-end integration tests with chaos (region latency spikes, pod preemption), iterate based on results
Week 5: Canary rollout (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollbacks on SLO regressions
testing_criteria: Unit tests for decision API math (SLO probability, headroom computation, weight normalization)
Integration tests that simulate uneven region capacity and validate weighted routing moves traffic with expected distribution
Chaos tests that induce a region capacity degradation and confirm circuit breaker trips within 30s and shedding reduces qps to safe levels
Load test: maintain client mix producing 20k rps to simulate peak load; confirm P0 token preservation and <3x increase in error rate for best-effort tier during controlled shedding
Canary monitoring: p50/p95/p99 latency trends, request success rate, region CPU/GPU utilization, and per-customer shed counts
observability_and_alerting: Console dashboard: SLO risk heatmap by region and customer tier
Alert: SLO risk > 0.25 for >3m in any region -> paging on-call reliability
Alert: circuit breaker open ratio > 0 for >2m -> auto-trigger investigation runbook
Metric: per-region headroom (numeric), and token-bucket depletion rate exposed as a gauge
Tracing: add tags for decision inputs (slo_risk, headroom, affinity_penalty, breaker_state) to request traces
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated in control plane for alpha teams
Alpha start with internal platform and three pilot customers with regional affinity requirements
Progressive ramp with automated SLO guard rails (rollback if p95 SLO breach probability increases by >10% over baseline)
Full default enablement gated behind runtime-1.22 release and completed security review
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect headroom estimates could cause premature shedding -> Mitigation: conservative two-minute smoothing and 'grace' capacity reservations
Risk: Affinity penalties may starve small regions -> Mitigation: minimum weight floor + scheduled rebuilds of weight based on customer contracts
Risk: False positives in circuit breakers during transient spikes -> Mitigation: dual-path breakers with hysteresis and exponential backoff before reopen
Risk: Observability gaps during rollout -> Mitigation: require dashboards and synthetic checks before canary advance
